result.what_interviewer_wanted: Explain that default arguments are evaluated once, so a mutable default like [] is shared across calls, leading to unintended state persistence, and how to fix it with None.
result.improved_answer: In Python, default arguments are evaluated only once when the function is defined. If you use a mutable default such as an empty list, that same list instance is reused on every call, so items added in one call persist into subsequent calls. The usual fix is to set the default to None and create a new list inside the function body.
